Nicknamed "'''Big Baby'''", he played for the [[Boston Celtics]], [[Orlando Magic]], [[Los Angeles Clippers]], and [[St. John’s Edge]]. After playing [[college basketball]] with the [[LSU Tigers basketball|LSU Tigers]], Davis was selected by the [[Seattle SuperSonics]] with the 35th overall pick in the [[2007 NBA draft]]. Shortly thereafter, he was traded to the Boston Celtics, with whom he won the [[2008 NBA Finals]]. ==Amateur career== Davis attended [[Louisiana State University Laboratory School]] in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. Considered a five-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Davis was listed as the No. 3 power forward and the No. 13 player in the nation in 2004.{{Cite web |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Glen-Davis-12936;_ylt=AghjgYmwi3UJsSYL.VpgnHtGPZB4 |title=Glen Davis Recruiting Profile |access-date=January 14, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160115001818/http://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Glen-Davis-12936 |archive-date=January 15, 2016 |url-status=dead }} Davis attended [[Louisiana State University]] (LSU) and played [[college basketball]] for the [[LSU Tigers men's basketball|LSU Tigers]]. The [[Southeastern Conference]]'s (SEC) coaches voted Davis the [[SEC Men's Basketball Player of the Year|2006 SEC Player of the Year]], and he was also named to the All-SEC first team. In 2006 as a [[Sophomore year|sophomore]], Davis led the Tigers to their first [[2006 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|Final Four]] appearance since 1986. In the crucial game of the national semifinals, LSU lost to [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]], trailing by a wide margin in the first half and never managing a comeback. Davis scored 17 points and made 4 out of 10 [[free throw]]s before eventually fouling out. ==Professional career== ===Boston Celtics (2007–2011)=== On March 20, 2007, Davis held a press conference to announce that he would forgo his junior season at LSU and enter his name into the [[2007 NBA draft]].{{cite web|url=https://news.yahoo.com/s/ap/20070320/ap_on_sp_co_ne/bkc_lsu_davis_1 |title=LSU's Glen Davis to enter NBA draft |publisher=Yahoo! Sports |date=March 20, 2007 |access-date=March 20, 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070328182451/http://news.yahoo.com/s/ap/20070320/ap_on_sp_co_ne/bkc_lsu_davis_1 |archive-date=March 28, 2007 |url-status=dead }} On March 20, 2007, it was reported that he had signed with agent John Hamilton of Performance Sports Management to represent him.{{cite web |title=LSU's 'Big Baby' Davis Going Pro |url=https://newsok.com/article/3029241/lsus-big-baby-davis-going-pro |website=NewsOK.com |access-date=August 27, 2018 |date=March 20, 2007}} Davis was drafted by the [[Seattle SuperSonics]] with the 35th overall pick in the [[2007 NBA draft]] behind [[Kevin Durant]] who was picked 2nd and [[Carl Landry]] who was picked 31st overall by the team. The rights to Davis and [[Ray Allen]] were traded to the [[Boston Celtics]] for [[Delonte West]], [[Wally Szczerbiak]], and the rights to the 5th overall pick in the 2007 NBA draft, [[Jeff Green (basketball)|Jeff Green]]. [[File:Glen Davis Celtics 2008.jpg|thumb|125px|left|Davis in Game 4 of the [[2008 NBA Playoffs]] against the [[Atlanta Hawks]]]] Davis was on the Celtics' 2007 [[National Basketball Association Summer League|summer league]] team. With the departures of [[Ryan Gomes]], [[Gerald Green]], and [[Al Jefferson]], Davis was expecting to see a lot of playing time his rookie season. Though he is primarily a power forward, Davis also spent some time playing as the team's backup center in the regular season.[http://celtics.bostonherald.com/celtics/view.bg?articleid=1009904 Not Playing Nice: Powe, Davis Enjoying a Battle of the Bigs]{{dead link|date=September 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} Steve Bulpett, the Boston Herald, July 6, 2007 After coming off [[Memphis, Tennessee|Memphis]].{{Cite web |title=Glen Davis 2008-09 Stats per Game - NBA - - ESPN (SG) |url=https://www.espn.com.sg/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/3200/year/2009 |access-date=2024-02-21 |website=- ESPN |language=en}} In the 2009 NBA Playoffs, Davis had significant playing time after injuries to Kevin Garnett and [[Leon Powe]]. In Game Four of the [[2009 NBA Playoffs#(2) Boston Celtics vs. (3) Orlando Magic|2009 Eastern Conference Semifinals]] against the [[Orlando Magic]], Davis made two key shots, including a buzzer beater, in the final seconds of the game to give the Celtics the 95–94 win over the Magic. After the shot, Davis accidentally jostled a twelve-year-old fan while running down the court in celebration. The boy's father complained to NBA and Celtics officials but later retracted his demand for an apology. Davis apologized nevertheless, and said that, "I'm a big guy. Imagine if my emotions are going so wild, and if I'm running by somebody, I don’t feel them. If I've hurt anybody or if I’ve done any harm to anybody, please forgive me because my intentions were harmless."Chad Finn, "[https://web.archive.org/web/20090515101649/http://www.boston.com/sports/basketball/celtics/extras/celtics_blog/2009/05/davis_im_sorry.html Davis: 'I'm sorry if I hurt anyone']," ''[[Boston Globe]]'', May 12, 2009. On August 10, 2009, Davis signed a two-year, $6.5 million contract with the Celtics.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/press_release/press081009-celtics-resign-glen-davis.html |title=Celtics Re-sign Glen Davis |work=[[NBA.com]] | date=August 10, 2009 |access-date=August 10, 2009}} On May 27, 2010, during the 2010 Eastern Conference Finals against the Orlando Magic in Game 5, Glen Davis suffered a severe concussion when he got elbowed in the face by [[Dwight Howard]]. Davis would play in the Game 6 clincher, finishing with 6 points and 7 rebounds as they advanced to the [[2010 NBA Finals]]. The Celtics would face the Los Angeles Lakers in a rematch of the 2008 championship. In Game 4, Davis had 18 points and 5 rebounds to tie the series. The Celtics fell in seven games. ===Orlando Magic (2011–2014)=== On December 12, 2011, Davis was signed and traded to the [[Orlando Magic]] along with [[Von Wafer]] for [[Brandon Bass]], signing a 4-year, $26 million contract.{{cite web | title = Magic Acquire Glen Davis and Von Wafer | url = http://www.nba.com/magic/news_davis_121211.html | work = [[NBA.com]] | date = December 12, 2011 | access-date = December 13, 2011 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120210000508/http://www.nba.com/magic/news_davis_121211.html | archive-date = February 10, 2012 | url-status = dead }} On April 3, 2012, Davis scored a then-career-high 31 points in a 95–102 loss to the Detroit Pistons. On December 3, 2013, he recorded a career high 33 points, along with 3 rebounds and 3 assists, in a double-overtime loss to the Philadelphia 76ers.{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20131203/ORLPHI/gameinfo.html |title=Notebook: Sixers 126, Magic 125 |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=December 4, 2013 Magic mutually agreed to a contract buyout.[http://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-glen-davis-agree-buyout Magic, Glen Davis Agree to Buyout] ===Los Angeles Clippers (2014–2015)=== On February 24, 2014, Zadar's side of the story...|url=https://basketball.hr/vijesti/tko-je-kriv-za-odlazak-davisa-zadarska-strana-price/6552 |publisher=basketball.hr |access-date=October 7, 2018 |date=October 6, 2018|language=hr}}{{cite web |title=VIDEO: Druga strana medalje – Big Baby u svojoj verziji priče krivi KK Zadar i trenera Aleša Pipana!|trans-title=VIDEO: The other side of the coin – Big Baby in his version of the story blames KK Zadar and coach Aleš Pipan!|url=https://basketball.hr/vijesti/video-druga-strana-medalje-big-baby-u-svojoj-verziji-price-krivi-kk-zadar-i-trenera-alesa-pipana/6555|publisher=basketball.hr |access-date=October 7, 2018 |date=October 6, 2018|language=hr}} On December 5, 2018, Davis signed with the [[St. John's Edge]] of the [[National Basketball League of Canada]].{{cite web |last1=Short |first1=Robin |title=St. John's Edge make "Big" signing |url=https://www.thetelegram.com/sports/st-johns-edge-make-big-signing-265639/ |website=[[The Telegram]] |access-date=December 5, 2018 |date=December 5, 2018}} In the 2018–19 season, Davis averaged 17.3 points, 7.4 rebounds, and 3.0 assists per game. He was named to the All-NBLC Third Team.{{cite web |title=NBLC Awards |url=http://nblcanada.ca/sports/mbkb/2017-18/NBLC_Awards |website=[[NBL Canada]] |access-date=November 30, 2019}} ==Personal life== In the summer of 2001, at only 15 years of age, Davis attended a basketball camp run by [[LSU Tigers basketball|LSU]] [[alumnus]] and future Boston Celtic teammate [[Shaquille O'Neal]] on the campus of [[Louisiana State University]]. O'Neal challenged Davis to a friendly wrestling match, in which Davis lifted the {{height|ft=7|in=1}}, {{convert|325|lb|kg st|abbr=on}} center and [[Professional wrestling throws#Body slam|body-slammed]] him to the ground. The encounter left a strong impression on O'Neal; ultimately, the incident helped Davis to get introduced to former LSU head coach [[Dale Brown (basketball)|Dale Brown]].Patrick Parker, [https://www.espn.com/nba/dailydime?page=dime-080327&lpos=spotlight&lid=tab4pos1 Shaq vs. Big Baby], ''[[ESPN.com]]'', March 27, 2008. His nickname is Big Baby,Steve Bulpett, [http://www.bostonherald.com/sports/basketball/celtics/view.bg?articleid=1069974&srvc=rss Big 3 minus an important two], ''[[Boston Herald]]'', January 30, 2008.[https://web.archive.org/web/20080203084158/http://scores.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=280129014 Powe, Rondo answer call for Celtics; Heat's Wade, Haslem leave game], ''[[Associated Press]]'', January 29, 2008. given to him at the age of 9 by a youth league coach. At {{height|ft=5|in=6}}, {{convert|160|lb|kg|abbr=on}}, he was too large to play pee-wee and played as a senior. When Davis felt he was being bullied by his older opponents, Davis' coach was known to say, "Stop crying, you big baby."{{cite news|last=Cannizzaro|first=Mark|title=It's 'Big Baby', not 'Baby Shaq'|url=http://www.nypost.com/p/sports/item_GzNPvcbce9MU1FTMmsXv5M|work=[[New York Post]]|date=March 20, 2006|access-date=April 23, 2010}} On December 21, 2008, Davis was injured in a car accident while driving to a game against the New York Knicks; he suffered a [[concussion]] and [[Whiplash (medicine)|whiplash]].[https://web.archive.org/web/20081225071441/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2008/basketball/nba/12/21/Davis.accident.ap/index.html Celtics' Glen Davis Injured in Accident] archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20130313161747/http://www.sportstalkflorida.com/insider-glen-davis-talks-about-his-injury/| archive-date = March 13, 2013| title = Insider: Glen Davis Talks production.[http://nesn.com/2016/11/glen-big-baby-davis-nba-career-on-hold-while-he-makes-movies-no-joke/ Glen ‘Big Baby’ Davis’ NBA Career ‘On Hold’ While He Makes Movies — No Joke] ===Legal issues=== On February 7, 2018, Davis was arrested for drug possession and drug distribution after police found 126 grams of marijuana, the equivalent of 6 packs of cigarettes, and a briefcase containing $92,000 in cash inside his hotel room in [[Aberdeen, Maryland]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/article/2018/03/17/glen-big-baby-davis-arrested-drug-charges|title=Former NBA player Glen "Big Baby" Davis arrested on drug charges|date=March 17, 2018|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|access-date=March 17, 2018}}{{Cite web |date=2018-03-17 |title=Glen 'Big Baby' Davis arrested on drug charges |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/22809694/former-nba-player-glen-davis-arrested-drug-charges |access-date=2025-01-24 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press |language=en}} Davis agreed to pay the maximum fine of $15,000 in exchange for moving the case to the stet docket, a legal disposition in the State of Maryland meaning the court agrees to indefinitely suspend the case and not pursue the charges.{{cite web|url= https://www.tmz.com/2019/02/15/glen-big-baby-davis-marijuana-weed-maryland-case/|title= EXCLUSIVE GLEN 'BIG BABY' DAVIS CUTS DEAL IN WEED CASE ... |date= February 15, 2019 |publisher=TMZ|access-date=March 28, 2020}} On October 7, 2021, Davis, along with 18 other former NBA players, were indicted by a federal grand jury in the [[Southern District of New York]] on charges of conspiracy to commit health care fraud and wire fraud for allegedly defrauding the NBA's health and welfare benefit plan. He is alleged to have filed fraudulent insurance claims for reimbursement.{{cite web| url = https://www.nbcnewyork.com/news/local/crime-and-courts/nba-veterans-arrested-in-alleged-health-insurance-fraud-scheme-sources/3311071/?_osource=db_npd_nbc_wnbc_twt_shr| title = 18 NBA Veterans Arrested in $4 Million Health Insurance Fraud Scheme – NBC New York| date = October 7, 2021}} On November 15, 2023, Davis was found guilty of committing health care fraud.{{cite news | last=John | first=Matt | title=Ex-Celtics Champion Glen Davis Found Guilty of Fraud: Report | date=November 15, 2023 | url=https://heavy.com/sports/boston-celtics/glen-davis-found-guilty-fraud-report/ | publisher=[[Heavy (website)|Heavy]] }} On May 9, 2024, Davis was sentenced to 40 months in prison, in addition to $80,000 in restitution. Davis was released from prison on March 12, 2026, and will enter the Long Beach Residential Reentry Management Office, more commonly known as a halfway house, until July 9, 2026. After he completes his time at the facility, Davis will face three years of supervised release.{{cite news | last=Prewitt | first=Alex | title=Glen 'Big Baby' Davis sentenced to 40 months in prison over fraud scheme | date=May 9, 2024 | url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/40113791/glen-big-baby-davis-sentenced-40-months-prison-fraud-scheme | work=ESPN }}{{Cite web |last=Musa |first=Ben
